standard.title: Volume and Capacity of Right Prisms
standard.description: solve problems involving the volume and capacity of right prisms using appropriate units
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can calculate volume of rectangular and triangular prisms using V = Ah (from AC9M7M02). Students understand unit conversion between cubic units and litres.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students solve problems involving volume and capacity of right prisms, selecting appropriate units and applying reasoning about optimal dimensions.

nodes.label: Unit relationships between volume and capacity
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students understand and apply the relationships 1 cm³ = 1 mL, 1000 cm³ = 1 L, 1 m³ = 1000 L, and use these to convert between volume and capacity units.
nodes.minimum_width: Convert between cm³ and mL, and between m³ and L, for given volumes.
nodes.typical_width: Apply unit conversion in practical problem contexts; choose appropriate units for the context; explain the relationship between cubic centimetres and millilitres.
wider: Investigate how unit choice affects the numerical value of a measurement — when is it more practical to use litres vs cubic metres in real contexts?
Explore the volume of a cubic metre using 1000 × 1000 mL = 1000 L as a concrete model — connect to large-scale water storage contexts.

response_modes.reason: Unit conversion between volume and capacity is a precision skill that students frequently get wrong under pressure. Fluency here is prerequisite to problem-solving.

nodes.hinge_reason: Unit conversion errors propagate directly into Node 2 — students who confuse cm³ and mL or m³ and L produce answers in the wrong unit or off by a factor of 1000 in practical capacity problems.
success_criteria: Correctly converts between cm³, mL, L and m³.
Selects appropriate units for a given practical context.
Does not confuse cm³ and cm (volume vs length).

nodes.label: Solving practical volume and capacity problems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students solve practical problems involving volume and capacity of right prisms, including optimisation and multi-step contexts.
nodes.minimum_width: Solve a practical problem requiring volume calculation and capacity interpretation.
nodes.typical_width: Apply volume reasoning to optimal packaging, production and dimension problems; interpret capacity in context; select which measurements matter for the problem.
wider: Investigate optimal packaging: for a fixed volume, what dimensions minimise surface area? Explore patterns for rectangular prisms.
Apply volume and capacity to a production context: given a required capacity and one fixed dimension, find the remaining dimension.

response_modes.reason: Practical volume problems vary significantly in what reasoning is needed — capacity problems, packaging optimisation, and dimension-finding all require recognising the same underlying formula but in different configurations.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Optimal packaging problems — minimising surface area for a fixed volume — offer advancing students a genuine optimisation investigation within the Year 8 band, connecting volume and area reasoning.
success_criteria: Selects and applies the correct formula for the prism type.
Interprets the result in context with appropriate units.
Identifies which measurements are relevant to the problem.
